title: fix(dedicated-autoscaler): backpressure metrics and burst reporting fix
author: Marina Lopez
release_notes: Fixes incorrect backpressure attribution in dedicated autoscaler reporting and corrects burst token accounting in utilization dashboard. No user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: Dedicated autoscaler reporting and backpressure signals were misattributing queued requests to the wrong priority buckets when burst tokens were consumed rapidly, causing downstream utilization dashboards to show inflated burst usage and SLO alerts to fire incorrectly. This PR fixes the attribution logic, adds additional unit and e2e tests, and improves observability for burst token consumption. Summary of changes: 1) Fix: correct priority->queue attribution path in autoscaler tokenbucket logic so backpressure events are recorded against the queue that actually delayed the request. 2) Fix: adjust burst token accounting to decrement in a single atomic step and emit a token_consumed metric with priority and shard labels. 3) Add: new metric dedicated.autoscaler.burst_tokens.consumed and dedicated.autoscaler.backpressure.events for clearer downstream reporting. 4) Add: end-to-end test that simulates sustained high QPS and burst exhaustion across priorities and verifies utilization and alert suppression. 5) Docs: update observability pack and dashboards to include the new metrics and a short note on interpreting burst vs sustained usage. CI: existing unit tests updated; integration harness now includes a synthetic workload scenario. Backwards compatibility: no API changes, metrics are additive. Rollout: safe to deploy behind a config flag that enables token_consumed emission; flag defaulted on for this rollout after canary.
